name: Netspace Thrill
description: Not a published list: built so the sweeps reach Kabonesa Wu: Netspace Thrillseeker, Kitara's Shaper identity, whose click searches the stack for a non-virus program and installs it 1[credit] cheaper, removing it from the game if it is still installed when the turn ends. On Level Pegging's list, its identity swapped; named to sort after every other deck, so the sweep schedule of those before it does not move. Kitara Stage 12f: two Compile for two Rejig, a run that installs a program from the stack or heap for nothing at its first encounter; Level Pegging keeps Rejig. Kitara Stage 15: two Flame-out for its two Tinkering, a host whose credits pay for the program on it. Kitara Stage 20 takes two Marathon for two Armitage Codebusting. Red Sand Stage 7 takes two Maven and two NanoTK for two Battering Ram and two Euler. Red Sand Stage 13 Network Exchange (Red Sand Stage 14) Red Sand Stage 19: two Dedicated Processor for two In the Groove, a mod hosted on a non-AI icebreaker that pumps it +4 for 2[credit]. Red Sand Stage 20: two Inversificator for two Living Mural, a decoder that swaps the ice it alone fully broke once it is passed. Mass-Driver (Red Sand Stage 21) takes Engolo's code gate slot Daredevil (Red Sand Stage 27) Red Sand Stage 53: one Adjusted Matrix for one NanoTK, a mod that lets its host break any subroutine for a click. Adept, Savant and Deep Data Mining are here for the unused memory they count (Flashpoint Stage 10).  FFG F6 Stage 1: a Harmony AR Therapy and a Beatriz Friere Gonzalez (each kept by other decks) for Temple of the Liberated Mind and Dr. Lovegood, one influence.
